title: Testing a home breath test to track asthma that gets worse around periods
official: A feasibility study of home-based longitudinal breath monitoring with Exhale-Dx to identify menstrual cycle linked respiratory signatures in premenopausal women with perimenstrual asthma in primary care
summary:
Background and study aims
Many women with asthma find their symptoms get worse around their period. This is called perimenstrual asthma, and it is linked to more asthma attacks and hospital visits. There is no simple, objective way to measure it. Exhale-Dx is a small device that analyses the gases and natural chemicals in breath while a person breathes normally for a few minutes. This study aims to find out whether women can use Exhale-Dx at home, and whether their breath changes in a regular way across the menstrual cycle.

Who can participate?
Women aged 18 to 50 with asthma who still have natural periods, notice their asthma gets worse around their period, and are registered at South Molton Medical Centre in Devon.

What does the study involve?
After a visit at the practice to give consent and learn how to use the device, each woman breathes into Exhale-Dx at home every day or every other day for three months. She also keeps a short diary of her symptoms, peak flow and period in an app, and fills in short questionnaires about her asthma and quality of life. The study team phones her a few times, and she has a final visit at three months. Her usual asthma care continues as normal.

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating?
There is no direct benefit expected, but the study may help develop a better way to monitor this type of asthma. The breath test is non-invasive and uses a new single-use mouthpiece each time. The main burden is the time spent on daily tests and the diary.

Where is the study run from?
South Molton Medical Centre (UK), with Breath Predict Ltd (UK) as sponsor. 

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for?
December 2026 to August 2027. 

Who is funding the study?
Innovate UK (UK)

Who is the main contact?
Dr Victor Higgs, vhiggs@breathpredict.com
conditions: Perimenstrual asthma that worsens around menstruation
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Female, aged 18 to 50 years
2. Doctor-diagnosed asthma recorded in the GP record, with at least one asthma medicine prescribed in the last 12 months
3. Pre-menopausal, with natural and reasonably regular menstrual cycles (21 to 35 days) over the last 3 months
4. Reports that asthma symptoms tend to worsen around menstruation
5. Registered with South Molton Medical Centre
6. Able and willing to use Exhale-Dx and the study app at home daily or on alternate days for 3 months and keep a symptom and menstrual diary
7. Able to give written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
1. Pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning pregnancy during the study
2. Using hormonal contraception, HRT or other treatment that changes the natural menstrual cycle
3. Asthma attack needing oral steroids, A&E or hospital admission in the last 4 weeks
4. Other significant lung disease (e.g. COPD, bronchiectasis, cystic fibrosis, interstitial lung disease)
5. Current chest infection
6. Current smoker or regular vaper
7. Hysterectomy, endometrial ablation or other condition/treatment that stops or seriously disrupts periods
8. Taking part in another interventional study that could affect asthma or breath results
9. Lacks capacity to consent
10. Any other reason the study GP considers would make participation unsafe or results unreliable
